Bijnor, whereby application dated 06.02.2024 under Sections 311 Cr.P.C. filed by applicant before court below to recall the witnesses has been rejected by court below.
4. At the very outset, the learned A.G.A. submits that notice of this application has been served upon first informant/opposite party-2 on 10.08.2024.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the impugned order dated 1.5.2024 has been passed without considering the facts and circumstances of the case.

It is further submitted that the applicant engaged a new counsel in the Special Case before the trial court and after engaging the new counsel, the applicant immediately filed an application under Section 311, Cr.P.C. with proposed questions, which are mostly related to confrontation of earlier statement of the victim, which have not been asked by earlier counsel for the applicant.

After perusal of the proposed questions, there are many questions left to be asked for confrontation from the victim with regard to her earlier statement recorded under Section 164, Cr.P.C.
Prima facie, matter requires consideration.
Learned A.G.A. has accepted notice on behalf of opposite party No. 1.

Issue notice to opposite party no.2 returnable at an early date.
Learned A.G.A. as well as opposite party no. 2 may file their counter affidavits within three weeks.
Rejoinder affidavit may be filed within one week thereafter.

sentences.text: Put up this case as fresh on 21.10.2024.
Till the next date of listing, further proceedings of the aforesaid case shall remain stayed against the applicant.
In compliance of above order dated 19.09.2024, notice was issued to first informant/opposite party-2.
As per office report dated 18.10.2024, notice issued to opposite party-2 has been received by Satish Kumar, the brother of first informant/opposite party-2.

However, irrespective of above, no counter affidavit has been filed by first informant/opposite party-2 nor anyone has put in appearance on his behalf to oppose this application, even in revised call.

7. Record shows that in respect of an incident, which is alleged to have occurred on 30.11.2021 a delayed F.I.R. dated 07.12.2021 was lodged by first informant/opposite party-2, Arjun Singh (father of the prosecutrix) and was registered as Case Crime No. 0683 of 2021 under Section 363 I.P.C.,
Police Station-Seohara, District-Bijnor.

In the aforesaid F.I.R. one person namely Krishna Kumar @
Kanhiya has been nominated as solitary named accused.
8. After aforementioned F.I.R. was lodged, Investigating Officer proceeded with statutory investigation of aforementioned case crime number in terms of Chapter XII Cr.P.C.
On the basis of material collected by the Investigating Officer during course of investigation, he came to the conclusion that offence complained of is prima-facie established.
Accordingly, the Investigating Officer opined to submit the charge sheet.

Resultantly, Investigating Officer submitted the police report (charge sheet) dated 20.12.2021 in terms of Section 173 (2) Cr.P.C whereby applicant was charge-sheeted under Sections 363, 376 I.P.C. and Sections 384 POCSO Act.
9.
Upon submission of aforementioned police report (charge sheet), cognizance was taken upon same by concerned court in exercise of jurisdiction under Section 190 (1) (b) Cr.P.C.

Resultantly,
trial of applicant before court below commenced.
The court concerned framed charges against applicant, who denied the same and pleaded innocence and also demanded trial.
Resultantly, trial procedure commenced before court below.
10. Prosecution in discharge of its burden to bring home the charges so framed against applicant adduced all the witnesses nominated in the charge sheet.

Subsequent to above, applicant filed an application dated 06.02.2024 under Section 311 Cr.P.C. praying therein that since the prosecutrix in her previous statements under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. had not supported the prosecution story but she has resiled from her previous statements in her deposition before court below.

Therefore,
the prosecutrix is required to be confronted by the defence with the same.

Accordingly, specific questions, which were desired to be put to the prosecutrix, were mentioned in the application under Section 311 Cr.P.C.
11.
Court below upon appraisal and appreciation of record, ultimately rejected the said application by means of the order impugned dated 01.05.2024.

sentences.text:
Thus feeling aggrieved by the above order dated 01.05.2024, applicant has now approached this Court by means of present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
13.

Learned counsel for applicant submits that perusal of application dated 06.02.2024 under Section 311 Cr.P.C. filed by accused/applicant before court below will go to show that clear and categorical questions proposed to be put to the prosecutrix have been clearly mentioned in the application itself.

The relevancy of the said questions is further evident from the fact that the prosecutrix in her previous statements under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. had not supported the F.I.R. He therefore submits that in the light of above, when the parameters laid by the Apex Court for judging the veracity of an application under Section 311 Cr.P.C. in Rajaram Prasad Yadav Vs.
State of Biharand Another, (2013) 14 SCC 461 is applied to the present case

sentences.text: , the application dated 06.02.2024 under Section 311 Cr.P.C. filed by accused/applicant was liable to be allowed.

Furthermore, in case the prosecutrix is recalled by court below and she is cross-examined on the questions so mentioned in the application under Section 311 Cr.P.C., the ultimate objective of the trial court i.e. to find out the truth as enunciated by the Apex Court in Versha Garg Vs. State of M.P.,
2022 SCC OnLine SC 986 shall be fulfilled.

sentences.text: As such, no prejudice can be said to be caused to the prosecutrix in case the application under Section 311 Cr.P.C. was allowed.
However, the court below in clear ignorance of the aforesaid settled principle of law has rejected the application filed by applicant.
As such, the order impugned dated 01.05.2024 passed by court below is liable to be quashed by this Court.
14. Per contra, the learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed this application.

Learned A.G.A.
contends that examination-in-chief of the prosecutrix commenced on 19.05.2023 and thereafter, the prosecutrix was cross-examined on behalf of accused.
The application under Section 311 Cr.P.C. was filed after expiry of a period of more than 7 months from the date examination-in-chief of the prosecutrix concluded.

Referring to the prohibition contained in Section 35 (5) of the POCSO Act,
the learned A.G.A. contends that no illegality has been committed by court below in rejecting the application under Section 311 Cr.P.C. filed by accused/applicant.
However, he could not dislodged the factual and legal submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicant in support of this application with reference to the record at this stage.

15. Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State and upon perusal of record this court finds that application dated 06.02.2024 under Section 311 Cr.P.C filed by accused/applicant before court below contains specific questions proposed to be put to the prosecutrix.

The relevancy of the said questions gains importance in view of the fact that the prosecutrix in her previous statements under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. has clearly not supported the prosecution story as unfolded in the F.I.R.
Furthermore, as per the mandate of law laid down in Section 144 of the Evidence Act, an accused can be confronted with her previous statements under Sections 161/164 Cr.P.C.
In view of above, in case the application under Section 311 Cr.P.C. was allowed no prejudice can be said to be caused to the prosecutrix.
As per law laid down by Apex Court in Versha Garg (Supra), the trial is that of the accused.
Such a trial should be a free and fair trial.
Furthermore, the ultimate objective is to find out the truth.
In case the application under Section 311 was allowed, the observations made by the Apex Court in Varsha Garg (Supra) could be fully complied with.

Apart from above, when the veracity of the application under Section 311 Cr.P.C.

Therefore, it is apparent that the application under Section 311 Cr.P.C. filed by accused/applicant before court below was bonafide.
As such, the same was liable to be allowed.
The Court below has, therefore, erred in law and fact in rejecting the same.
16. In view of the discussions made above, the present application succeeds and is liable to be allowed.
17. It is accordingly allowed.

Upon such deposit being made, the court below shall recall the prosecutrix, P.W.-2 for her further cross-examination.
The amount deposited by the applicant before court below in compliance of this order shall be paid to the prosecutrix.
It is however made clear that only one opportunity shall be available to the accused/applicant to cross-examine the prosecutrix in respect of the questions proposed to be put to the prosecutrix.

However, if on any ground, applicant fails to cross-examine the prosecutrix on the next date fixed by court below for further cross-examination of the prosecutrix, the right of accused/applicant to cross-examine the prosecutrix in terms of this order
